newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bank of New Zealand launches new retail unit trust.
newsitem.headline: Bank of New Zealand launches new retail unit trust.

text.p: Bank of New Zealand on Wednesday launched a new retail unit trust designed to track the movements of the NZSE-40 capital index.
The bank said the launch of the BNZ New Zealand Equity Index Trust made it first in the market with index-tracking funds for both retail and wholesale investors.

The new trust will invest in shares that comprise the BNZ 25 equity index. The bank launched its wholesale BNZ 25 equity index fund (a superannuation fund for wholesale/institutional investors) earlier this month and this, too, invests in shares that comprise the BNZ 25.

BNZ Financial Services Group General Manager David Jones said today's tax environment clearly favoured passive index-tracking funds like the two BNZ funds, both of which enjoyed the added certainty of binding rulings from New Zealand's Inland Revenue protecting them from capital gains tax on the sale of shares.
"We view these new index funds as important additions to our wide stable of investment alternatives, which all utilise our disciplined investment methodology," he said.

"Since the first index-tracking funds were introduced in New Zealand last July, over NZ$300 million has been invested into them. It's impossible to ignore the tax advantages of these funds, and they can effectively complement actively-managed equity funds and all other asset clases of investment."
The BNZ 25 has been constructed by BNZ Investment Management Ltd following analysis of the more commonly-known sharemarket indices such as the NZSE-10, NZSE-30 and NZSE-40.
BNZ said it had been constructed to closely replicate the NZSE-40 with a low tracking error, and to minimise transaction costs, thereby providing enhanced returns.
